Subject: Optimize economics & quantization guidance for Beacon Health deployment

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the quick intro call yesterday. As discussed, Beacon's real-time summarization and triage workload looks like a great fit for Redwood's Optimize toolkit. Before we jump into a POC, wanted to share a short note on pricing structure options we recommend based on the workload shape you mentioned (short sessions, median seq len ~180 tokens, ~420k tokens/day).

High-level recommendations:
- Quantization: start with q8_0 for the encoder model path; fall back to int8 for heavy tails. That keeps inference quality within ~1–2% of fp16 for summarization while saving ~2.2–2.6x cost on GPU time.
- Batching/cache: target burst batch sizes of 8–24 for 95th% latency < 350ms; enable prefix KV caching for multi-message sessions to reduce recomputation by ~30–50%.
- Credits & packaging: we typically offer tiered committed credits with stepped discounts (3%, 7%, 12%) at milestone tiers: 10M / 30M / 75M monthly tokens. For Dedicated commits we can offer an additional 5% price concession and a custom quantization profile.

I've attached a short package summary and a sample cost model that maps to the telemetry you shared. If you want, I can loop in Monica (Customer Success) and Dev (Solutions Eng) to build a small mutual action plan + POC scope that includes a token-level cost projection and SLO targets.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Confirm procurement windows + target start date for a 4-week POC (we can make it a no-cost pilot for the first 2 weeks with usage caps).
2) Share a sample subset of traffic (anonymized) so Dev can produce an expected tokens/sec profile.
3) Decide target committed credits for tier discount modeling.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Emma / Jason —

Thanks for the clear asks — I put together a compact response below and attached a numeric model that maps our unit economics to the two quantization paths. Key points:

1) Token price examples (hosted API, post-discount example numbers are illustrative):
- q8_0 path (recommended starter): base list: $2.30 per 1M tokens.
  - With 10M monthly commit (annualized): 3% discount => $2.231/M
  - With 30M monthly commit: 7% discount => $2.139/M
- int8 path (aggressive cost): base list: $1.05 per 1M tokens (lower latency but more variance).
  - With 30M commit: 7% discount => $0.976/M
Notes: Pricing above bundles inference time, caching savings, and typical batching. The attached Beacon_MVP_cost_model.xlsx runs your 420k tokens/day through both paths and shows the expected monthly spend.

2) Discount structure & pilot concession:
- We can do a time-bound ramp agreement: 45-day pilot with a provisional 30M monthly credit commitment at a pilot rate (7% discount). If Beacon elects to convert to a 12-month reserved commit within 30 days of pilot close, we will credit back the incremental difference up to the 12% tier retroactively. In plain terms: pilot friendly + ability to lock a better rate after successful POC.

3) SLOs & deployment options:
- Hosted (standard): 95th% latency target under 500ms for requests under seq len 256 with recommended batching settings; SLA add-on available for 99.9% uptime and response latency credits.
- Dedicated: we can guarantee 95th% under 350ms with reserved capacity and prioritized routing. Dedicated also reduces noisy-neighbor variance and is what we recommend for your patient triage workload if you need hard latency bounds.

4) Technical recommendations for the POC:
- Batching: start with target batch sizes 12–18; auto-batch with a 40ms coalescing window.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for patient session context (expect ~35% token reduction for repeated context).
- Quantization fallback: run q8_0 by default and route long-tail/edge cases to int8 fallback nodes to keep latency predictable.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm pilot window and usage cap (I suggest 45 days, capped at 1.5M tokens/day).
- Monica will drive the onboarding checklist. Dev will produce a short perf-run using an anonymized snippet you provide.
- I'll open a HubSpot MAP and draft the provisional term sheet for procurement review.

If that sounds good I'll prepare the MAP link and a short one-pager for legal/procurement.

Best,
Rishi
